_meta.target: calibrated_point = headline correct-rate in ~[0.1, 0.35]; sweep spans ~0.9 -> ~0.0

tsp.notes: Beyond n=13 tours stay valid (value ~0.93-0.95) but never optimal; gradated ratio is the metric past the cliff.

maze.notes: Pooled rounds 1+2; high seed variance. Cliff is at/below size 6 - easy rungs (4, 5) added to sweep, unmeasured. Failures are invalid moves (wall hits, stopping short), not suboptimality.

sat.notes: Very sharp cliff between n=6 and n=7. Dominant failure: claims SAT with a broken assignment (label=invalid) - the certificate asymmetry working as designed.

argmax.notes: Exact-argmax correct-rate; gradated value stays 0.55-0.8 past the cliff (model finds good-not-best points). Easy end requires single-mode functions.

chaos.notes: NO HEADROOM BELOW k=1: a single logistic iteration (one 6-digit multiply chain) is already at the cliff for 4-decimal exactness. Henon k=1 is the easy rung (gentler arithmetic). Consider a 3-decimal variant if an easier rung is ever needed; digits-based gradated value is the primary metric for this family.

automata.notes: k=2 vs k=3 non-monotonic at these sample sizes (n=10/6) - noise; cliff band is k=2-4. Hamming-fraction value declines smoothly (0.85 -> 0.53 by k=8).
